items.undo: A soft delete (deleted_at) can be reversed; a hard delete cannot. The method has not been chosen.

items.title: The repeated embedding-refusal log rows
items.rule: Rows where the destination is the embedding door, the status is refused, the reason starts awaiting_email_approval, the row is older than 24 hours, and a newer row for the same account, feature and approval key exists. The newest refusal of each distinct question stays, and so does everything from the last day. Rows that were sent, intended or failed are never selected.
items.why: A correct refusal was written again and again by a loop. The record that the door asked and was not answered stays; only the repetition goes.

claim.source: Card q1015 ('about 219,000 log rows'); production was not read when it was written.

items.undo: A hard delete cannot be undone. Only the backup file brings the rows back.

items.title: Exact copies in the memory table
items.rule: Live rows that are identical to an earlier live row on account, kind, type, source, family, privacy tier, event time, event id and the whole payload. In each group the row that already has an embedding is kept, then the lowest id. Rows that differ in any of those columns are not copies and are kept.
items.why: The same fact was written more than once. Copies count twice in search and in the corpus census.

claim.source: Card q1015 ('about 20,238 duplicates and old test rows') and the product checklist X6 (10.2 percent of the corpus). Production was not read.

items.undo: Soft delete sets deleted_at and search already skips such rows, so it can be reversed by clearing deleted_at.

items.title: Test conversations in the NovahPrime database
items.store: the local NovahPrime database on this PC
items.rule: Conversations whose title matches 'selftest', or whose messages contain the scripted prompts 'run the tools', 'give me a long answer' or 'permission please'. This is a guess by wording: a real chat that used one of those phrases would be caught too, so the titles must be read first.
items.why: The test run that made them is fixed, but the 80 conversations it left are still searchable and waiting to be embedded and copied.
